[opencode plugin] Routing policy — Claude conducts, OpenCode Go executes. This is COST-AWARE delegation, NOT "delegate everything".

WHEN to delegate to opencode:
- Bulk / parallel / repetitive work that clearly exceeds the spec + round-trip + verify overhead: mass scaffolding, exhaustive test generation, migrations, long-context reads that return a small digest, fan-out search.
- Tools Claude can use via opencode: web search (webfetch) when enabled.
WHEN NOT to: small, self-contained, or judgement-heavy tasks — do them yourself. Delegating a tiny task is a measured NET LOSS.

HOW (the cost levers):
- Call: `oc-delegate` [--tier flash|code|pro] [--dir <repo>] [--write] "<task>" — or use the opencode-delegate subagent so file generation happens on the cheap model and does not spend Claude tokens.
- Keep Claude's context LEAN (biggest lever): take a DIGEST; never re-read the files opencode handled or paste its raw output back into the thread.
- Pass --dir <repo-root> so opencode reads AGENTS.md + the real files instead of pasted context. Batch one big delegation over many small ones. Review the diff, not the whole tree.
- Headless (claude -p): delegate SYNCHRONOUSLY — there is no later turn to collect a backgrounded result.
- Dollar-based quota: ~$12/5h, ~$30/wk, ~$60/mo. Tier choice IS quota management — flash for bulk, code for implementation, pro (scarce) for hard reasoning.

VERIFY (non-negotiable): never trust opencode's self-reported "GREEN" — actually run the gate yourself. Claude owns correctness.

Small one-off edits do not need delegation. Full detail is in the `opencode` skill. Turn this notice off via the plugin's `coding_policy` option.
